hero.heading: Media & Press
hero.subtitle: For journalists, researchers, and documentarians looking to cover the Heal Gurukuli Initiative, our therapeutic methods, or the history of institutional abuse within gurukulas.

pressOffice.heading: Press Office & Spokesperson
pressOffice.body: We accommodate interview requests and statements regarding clinical support, safeguarding, and recovery frameworks. To coordinate interviews with our founder Caitanya Lila or external clinical advisors, please submit an inquiry.
pressOffice.note: Note: We will never disclose patient identities, clinical data, or active treatment details under any circumstance.
pressOffice.responseNote: Response within 4 hours for urgent breaking news.

guidelines.heading: Ethical Reporting Guidelines
guidelines.intro: Reporting on institutional child abuse and complex PTSD requires extreme sensitivity. When covering these topics, we urge journalists to follow these guidelines:

items.title: 1. Protect Anonymity
items.body: Many adult survivors reside in close-knit communities where exposure would cause social or professional disruption. Always verify consent before disclosing names, locations, or family ties.

items.title: 2. Avoid Sensationalism
items.body: Focus on systemic institutional failure, clinical recovery frameworks, and therapeutic resources rather than detailed descriptions of abuse that may act as trauma triggers.

items.title: 3. Frame Around Agency
items.body: Represent survivors as active agents in their own recovery, rather than passive victims. Highlight clinical progress and community initiatives.

items.title: 4. Provide Help Resources
items.body: Always close your articles or broadcasts with details for national support helplines (such as Samaritans, child protection lines, or our resource page link).
